subject: POC SLO scoping: end-to-end p95/p99 targets & test plan
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@nimbushealth.com>, Priyanka Shah <pshah@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: POC SLO scoping: end-to-end p95/p99 targets & test plan

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope a short POC to validate end-to-end latency and concurrency behavior.

Summary of what we heard from you on the call:
- Primary traffic: interactive patient-facing text generation (small prompts, average ~40 output tokens)
- Current expectations: p95 and p99 are decision gates for go/no-go on hosted switching
- Target production concurrency: ~50 concurrent user sessions per region, sustained throughput ~200 qps with occasional bursts to 350 qps
- Streaming: you asked about streaming for progressive tokens; not currently used but interested for perceived latency improvements

Proposed POC scope (72-hour run):
1) Baseline collection — we need current provider p95/p99 numbers across your normal traffic profile (can you share a 48h sample or summary?)
2) Redwood hosted POC — run a 72-hour test with a controlled traffic replay (we can mimic 200 qps steady ramping to 350 qps bursts, and a streaming vs non-streaming comparison)
3) Success criteria — p95 <= 200ms end-to-end and p99 <= 450ms for hosted API for the primary text-gen path; throughput and error-rate should be comparable or better than current provider
4) Deliverables — latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), concurrency behavior, cost delta estimate, and recommended runtime config (batching/quantization)

Attachments: SLO_playbook_v1.pdf (POC checklist), streaming_requirements_checklist.xlsx (we'll use this to capture expectations).

Questions / asks from your side:
- Please share current provider p95/p99 and an anonymized traffic sample (or a summary CSV)
- Confirm a 3-day window you can support for the POC and who on your side will own traffic shaping/procurement

If that aligns, we’ll schedule the POC kickoff and loop in Karthik (solutions) to handle the traffic harness and runtime tuning.

Best,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@nimbushealth.com>

Cc: Priyanka Shah <pshah@nimbushealth.com>, procurement@nimbushealth.com
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 17:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC SLO scoping: end-to-end p95/p99 targets & test plan

Sofia — thanks for the clear recap. Agrees with the plan. Quick answers to your asks below and a few clarifying notes.

Current provider baseline (last 7 days, production):
- p95 (text-gen, full end-to-end including our API gateway): ~420ms
- p99 (same path): ~980ms
- Typical payload: prompt ~30–60 input tokens, average response ~40 tokens
- We do not currently use streaming in prod, only full-response APIs
- Concurrency: we typically observe ~40–60 concurrent active sessions per region during peak; average steady qps ~180–220 with spikes to ~340 for short windows

POC details:
- We can provide a 48h anonymized request log (CSV) and a lightweight traffic replay harness on our side.
- Procurement (cc'd) will need an SOW and PII/BAA confirmation if we proceed beyond POC.
- Proposed POC window: we can support Oct 10–12 for a 72-hour run.

Two questions for Redwood: 
1) How do you measure end-to-end? Does your p95 include our edge gateway? We prefer the measurement to reflect our real path (client -> our gateway -> Redwood -> client).
2) Can you run a streaming vs non-streaming head-to-head during the POC? We want to understand perceived latency improvements and any tradeoffs in cost.

On timing — if Oct 10–12 works, we’ll aim to share the logs by Oct 4 so your team can prep.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Director of Platform Engineering, Nimbus Health
alex.johnson@nimbushealth.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@nimbushealth.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC SLO scoping: end-to-end p95/p99 targets & test plan

Alex / Sofia — Karthik from Solutions here. Thanks for the details, Alex — very helpful. Couple of technical clarifications and our proposed runtime configuration for the POC so we can set expectations.

How we measure end-to-end: our preferred approach is to instrument a lightweight client-side header (x-redwood-trace-id) that will let us correlate client request time at your gateway with the final token delivered back to the client. That gives a true client-to-client p95/p99. If adding the header is difficult, we can also support server-side timing anchored at the Redwood ingress but will flag that as a slightly optimistic measurement.

Streaming vs non-streaming: we can run both during the POC. Streaming typically improves perceived latency (first-byte) but may not significantly change p99 for large outliers unless prefix caching applies. We'll run a split traffic test: 50% streaming, 50% non-streaming.

Recommended POC runtime config (initial):
- Two warm worker groups in us-west with autoscale headroom for burst to 3x baseline
- Continuous micro-batching with max batch size tuned to 16 tokens/request (auto-adapt)
- KV prefix caching enabled for repeated prompt patterns you mentioned
- Quantized model variant for cost-performance tradeoff (we'll surface exact delta in report)
- Concurrency handling: we’ll emulate 50 concurrent sessions and ramp qps 180 -> 350 during the run

Expected ballpark (based on your traffic profile and our hosted runtime):
- Expected hosted p95 (client-to-client): ~120–180ms for non-streaming first-response in single-region run
- Expected hosted p99 (client-to-client): ~320–450ms for the same configuration; streaming will shift p50/p95 lower but p99 depends on tail causes (network, gateway)

We will prepare a small load-test harness (attached: load-test-harness.zip) and a step-by-step POC runbook. As Sofia noted, deliverables will include p50/p95/p99 breakdowns, cost delta, and recommended fallback policies.

Action items:
- Alex: share anonymized logs & a sample CSV by Oct 4
- Redwood (Karthik/Sofia): provision POC infra and share runbook by Oct 7
- Procurement: we’ll surface a short SOW for the POC (no long-term commitment)

Thanks — I’ll sync with Sofia and Monica to schedule the kickoff.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Best,
Alex
